leaders.priorInstitution: Abilene Christian University (same institution; he had been executive assistant to the president before moving into the provost role in 1988)
leaders.notes: Tenth president and the person in office at the 1996 scope boundary; an internal promotion who succeeded William J. Teague in 1991. Stepped down as president in 2010 and moved into the newly created chancellor role, which he still holds. A Church of Christ minister by training, his tenure included the controversial 2006 unaccompanied-singing worship service that drew national religious-press attention.

leaders.priorInstitution: Abilene Christian University (same institution; he joined the administration as chief financial officer in 1998)
leaders.notes: Eleventh and current president, a 1991 ACU graduate and fully internal appointment; announced February 12, 2010 and took office June 1, 2010, succeeding chancellor-bound Royce Money. In 2014 trustees publicly considered but declined to remove him over his divorce and remarriage, a widely covered episode in Christian-college media. No presidential search is active as of mid-2026.

Seventh president and the person in office at the 1996 scope boundary. His tenure ended in a highly public governance crisis: the New York Board of Regents removed nearly all of Adelphi's trustees in February 1997 for failing to rein in his high compensation and management style, and the reconstituted board fired him February 21, 1997. He sued and settled for $1.4 million, then was hired in December 1998 by BU president John Silber, a personal friend, remaining until retirement in 2008. Died 2015.

leaders.priorInstitution: Adelphi University (same institution; appointed provost by Diamandopoulos)
leaders.notes: Under Adelphi's bylaws the sitting provost was next in line, but the reconstituted board considered him too closely tied to Diamandopoulos for a permanent role and launched an outside search rather than confirm him; he is nonetheless the officially documented bridge between Diamandopoulos's February 1997 ouster and Matthew Goldstein's June 1998 arrival. Exact start/end dates and his formal title during this period (acting vs. interim) could not be confirmed from a contemporaneous news source, so this entry is inferred from Wikipedia's succession listing for the presidency; he continued afterward as a tenured English professor.

External hire (eighth president), in office since June 1998 following the extended 1997-98 leadership search that started with Diamandopoulos's dismissal; came directly from seven years as president of Baruch College. His Adelphi tenure was brief: he was named CUNY chancellor and left September 1, 1999, going on to lead the 24-campus CUNY system until 2013.

leaders.priorInstitution: Adelphi University (same institution; also former publisher of New York Newsday and chief of staff to NYC Mayor John Lindsay)
leaders.notes: Named interim president when Goldstein departed abruptly for CUNY in fall 1999, drawing on his own board leadership through the post-Diamandopoulos reforms; served until Robert A. Scott's arrival in July 2000. A journalist and former mayoral aide with an Ivy League and Oxford background, he later led PEN American Center and taught at several universities.

Ninth president and an external hire, effective July 1, 2000 after 15 years leading Ramapo College; widely credited with stabilizing and rebuilding Adelphi's reputation and finances after the Diamandopoulos era. Stepped down June 30, 2015 and remained affiliated as president emeritus and university professor, later doing higher-ed consulting work.

Tenth president and Adelphi's first woman president, external hire effective July 1, 2015 from the provost's office at the University of Kentucky. Stepped down June 20, 2025 after nearly a decade in the role; no public reason was given for her departure, and her next role has not been announced.

Internal caretaker appointment, named interim president effective immediately upon Riordan's June 20, 2025 departure while the board ran a national search for the 11th president; served until Michael Balboni's June 1, 2026 start. Previously led Adelphi through COVID-era academic continuity and faculty bargaining as provost.

leaders.priorInstitution: Adelphi University (same institution; also founder of RedLand Strategies, a public-safety consulting firm, and a former New York State Senator and Deputy Secretary for Public Safety)
leaders.notes: Eleventh president, effective June 1, 2026; a 1981 Adelphi alumnus and the first alumnus, first parent and first Long Islander to hold the office. Career politician turned private-sector consultant, he moved directly from chairing Adelphi's board of trustees into the presidency, an internal-to-the-board but externally unconventional transition.

leaders.nextRole: Retired (first retirement); later returned to ASU as interim president
leaders.notes: Tenth president and the person in office at the 1996 scope boundary; external hire who had earlier been president of Paine College (1982-1988) and Texas Southern University (1988-1993). Took office at ASU June 1, 1994 and announced his retirement in April 2000, leaving effective September 30, 2000, the first of what became three separate stints leading the university. Died 2024.

Bridged the gap between Harris's September 2000 retirement and Joe A. Lee's 2001 arrival. His title/role immediately before and after the interim presidency could not be verified from an available online source.

Eleventh president, an external hire from the presidency of Tougaloo College in Mississippi (1995-2001), after decades at Talladega College. Oversaw a $125 million campus building campaign but presided over the controversial dismissal of head football coach L.C. Cole, and resigned abruptly, effective May 31, 2008, catching trustees off guard. Died 2024.

Second stint; brought back and installed July 14, 2008 to replace the abruptly departed Joe Lee. Served until Joseph Silver's appointment in September 2012, then was called back again as interim president that December after Silver's ouster.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Thirteenth president, external hire named June 2012; his brief tenure (September-December 2012) ended when the board and Silver parted ways in December 2012 after he alleged corrupt dealings by trustees and executive staff, a rupture that triggered public alumni petitions demanding his reinstatement.

Third and final stint leading the university, called back as interim president in December 2012 after Silver's departure and serving until Gwendolyn Boyd took office in February 2014. Retired from higher education administration afterward; died 2024.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Assistant to the Chief of Staff
leaders.priorInstitution: Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory
leaders.notes: Fourteenth president and ASU's first woman president; an alumna and external hire from a long engineering-management career at Johns Hopkins' Applied Physics Laboratory, announced December 2013 and took office February 2014. The board voted 8-6 to terminate her contract in December 2016, citing loss of confidence, amid controversy over a Steve Harvey event contract and a relocated high-school basketball tournament; her subsequent role is not publicly documented.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.priorInstitution: Alabama State University (same institution; dean of the College of Liberal Arts and Sciences from 2011)
leaders.nextRole: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Internal caretaker appointment as the sitting provost stepped up when Boyd was suspended and then fired in December 2016, serving until Quinton Ross took office in October 2017, then resumed the provost role.

leaders.priorTitle: Alabama State Senator (District 26) and Senate Minority Leader
leaders.notes: Fifteenth and current president, an ASU alumnus who resigned his state Senate seat on October 2, 2017 to take office October 3, 2017 after the board elected him 12-2. A veteran Montgomery-area legislator (elected 2002, minority leader 2014-2017), he was later appointed to the NCAA's top governing body in 2024. No presidential search is active.

leaders.priorInstitution: Universidad Carlos Albizu (same institution, then Puerto Rico Institute of Psychology)
leaders.notes: Second president of the institution (both the San Juan and Miami campuses, unified as Carlos Albizu University in January 2000) and the person effectively in office at the 1996 scope boundary; took over in January 1985 after founder Carlos Albizu Miranda's October 1984 death and won APA accreditation for three doctoral programs. His exact departure date is not confirmed by an independent source; 2007 is inferred as the year his successor, Ileana Rodríguez García, is documented as taking office. Very sparse English-language documentation exists for this leadership tier; Puerto Rico-based Spanish-language sourcing was used.

Terminated January 15, 2014 with only six days' notice instead of the 90 days her contract required; she sued and the Puerto Rico Supreme Court ruled in 2018 that the university had wrongfully dismissed her, awarding roughly $398,000 in back pay plus attorney's fees through the contract's September 2015 expiration. Her prior role before 2007 and subsequent career after 2014 could not be verified.

External hire named June 3, 2014 after resigning his University of Puerto Rico governing-board post; presided over a dysfunctional board of trustees, including a August 2015 mass resignation of trustees who accused the board majority of illegally cutting him out of budget decisions amid a stalled, over-budget construction project. His end date and next role are not confirmed by an independent source; 2016 is inferred as the year before Jose Pons is documented taking office in January 2017.

leaders.priorTitle: Founding Dean, School of Behavioral and Neural Sciences
leaders.notes: Fifth president, named by the Board of Trustees in January 2017; oversaw the university's later rebrand to simply "Albizu University." Announced his retirement effective December 31, 2021.

leaders.priorTitle: Rector and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: Sixth and current president of Albizu University, an external hire effective August 8, 2022; a Puerto Rican/Latino educator who previously held faculty and administrative posts at Indiana University-Purdue University Indianapolis, the University of Missouri and the University of Cincinnati. Whether an interim covered the roughly seven-month gap after Pons's December 2021 retirement could not be confirmed. Day-to-day leadership of the Miami campus specifically now sits with a campus Chancellor, a newly created position first filled on an interim basis by Sharrie R. Dean (from October 2022) and then permanently by Yianni Vassiliou (from January 2025); that role reports to Soto rather than replacing the university presidency.
